GRU4Rec’s official implementation recommends comparing BPR-max with cross-entropy and reports that sampling correction (`logq=1`) usually helps cross-entropy. BPR-max already emphasizes high-scoring negatives through softmax weighting; additional hard mining may therefore offer limited benefit. These findings support testing the objective before increasing recurrent capacity, but do not establish the cause of weak Electronics separation. [Official GRU4Rec](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec). A 2025 sampled-softmax paper identifies a correction subtlety: the positive is always included, so its denominator contribution should not receive the same Monte Carlo correction as sampled negatives. [Correcting the LogQ Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).

Hard negatives also risk being unobserved positives. UFNRec (2023) demonstrates that false negatives contain useful preference information; this supports caution about aggressive mining, without requiring its label-reversal machinery here. [UFNRec](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611977653.ch6). A 2024 sequential-recommendation study finds sampling effects depend on dataset popularity structure, with aggregate metrics masking head/tail trade-offs. [Sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276). Feasible hypothesis: preserve the corrected GRU4Rec, sampler, architecture, and training schedule; replace BPR-max with importance-corrected sampled softmax using the actual training-only proposal probabilities, masking padding and accidental target collisions. Change sampling separately afterward to distinguish objective effects from negative-distribution effects.

Select using the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, reporting Electronics alongside the other categories; larger raw margins are insufficient evidence. Sampled metrics can reverse model ordering relative to full-catalog evaluation, so any gain applies specifically to the pinned 99-negative protocol. Keep the host evaluator unchanged and one trained checkpoint per category. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).
